literal: Dezheng again poured out his heart and firmly pressed the request.
idiomatic: Dezheng again laid bare his heart and pressed the matter without relenting.

literal: The emperor then wrote in his own hand to Yang Yin, setting forth in full the men's intent in urging accession.
idiomatic: Gao Yang then wrote in his own hand to Yang Yin, explaining in full how the others meant to urge him onto the throne.

literal: Dezheng feared Yin would still hesitate and not decide; he asked leave to ride post-haste to the capital on other business as a pretext, speaking only with Yang Yin — and Yin at last echoed him.
idiomatic: Dezheng feared Yin would still waver; he asked to ride post-haste to the capital on a pretext of other business and spoke with Yin alone — and Yin at last fell in with him.

literal: Before Dezheng could return, the emperor had already set out from Jinyang, reached the fortress at Pingcheng, summoned the meritorious generals in, and told them of the abdication.
idiomatic: Before Dezheng returned, Gao Yang had already left Jinyang, reached the fortress at Pingcheng, summoned the meritorious generals, and told them of the abdication.

literal: The generals heard it suddenly; all were stunned, and none dared answer.
idiomatic: The generals heard it all at once and stood stunned; none dared speak.

literal: At the time Du Bi was chief clerk; he secretly reported to Gao Yang: "Guanxi is the state's formidable foe. If you now accept Wei's abdication, I fear they will raise a righteous army, take the Son of Heaven in hand, and march east — how will Your Highness meet them?"
idiomatic: Du Bi was chief clerk at the time; he secretly reported to Gao Yang, "Guanxi is the state's hard enemy. If you accept Wei's abdication now, I fear they will call it a righteous army, take the Son of Heaven in hand, and march east — how will you meet them?"

literal: Gao Yang entered and summoned Bi in to tell Xu Zhicai together.
idiomatic: Gao Yang went in and summoned Bi to tell Xu Zhicai together.

literal: Xu Zhicai said: "He who contends with you for the realm today likewise means to become emperor — like chasing a rabbit through a crowded market: once one man catches it, every heart is settled."
idiomatic: Xu Zhicai said, "Whoever contends with you for the realm today wants to be emperor too — like chasing a rabbit through a crowded market: once one man catches it, every heart settles."

literal: If you accept Wei's abdication first, Guanxi should of itself quiet its heart.
idiomatic: Accept Wei's abdication first and Guanxi should quiet of itself.

literal: Even if they wish to bend their strength against us, at most they will chase us in proclaiming emperorship.
idiomatic: Even if they mean to force the issue, at most they will chase us in declaring themselves emperor.

literal: You must seize the moment and be first to perceive the chance — no room to learn from others afterward."
idiomatic: You must know the moment and move first — no learning from others after the fact."

literal: Bi had nothing to answer.
idiomatic: Bi had nothing to say.

literal: The emperor had already sent post-horses toward Ye with letters to Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, Army Supervisor Lou Rui, Palace Attendant Zhang Liang, Yellow Gate Zhao Yanshen, Yang Yin, and others.
idiomatic: Gao Yang had already sent post-horses toward Ye with letters to Grand Commandant Gao Yue, Director of the Masters of Writing Gao Longzhi, army supervisor Lou Rui, palace attendant Zhang Liang, yellow gate Zhao Yanshen, Yang Yin, and the rest.

literal: Yue and the others rode express to the Gaoyang post-station; the emperor sent word: "I know what you nobles intend — no need to come."
idiomatic: Yue and the others rode express to the Gaoyang post-station; Gao Yang sent word, "I know what you nobles intend — you need not come."

literal: Only Yang Yin was received; Gao Yue and the rest all returned.
idiomatic: Only Yang Yin was received; Gao Yue and the others all turned back.

literal: The emperor, because the men's hearts were not yet aligned, had also earlier received the empress dowager's charge: "Your father was like a dragon, your brother like a tiger — and both ended as subjects. How can you think to play Yao and Shun?"
idiomatic: Because the men's hearts were not yet one, Gao Yang had also received the empress dowager's word earlier: "Your father was like a dragon and your brother like a tiger, yet both died as subjects — how can you think to play Yao and Shun?"

literal: This is not your own thought either; it is Gao Dezheng who is teaching you."
idiomatic: This is not your thought either; it is Gao Dezheng teaching you."

literal: Others also urged that in old times King Wu of Zhou crossed the Meng Ford twice before he began the revolution — and so he turned back to Jinyang.
idiomatic: Others said that in old times King Wu of Zhou crossed the Meng Ford twice before he began the revolution — and so he turned back to Jinyang.

literal: From then on he was habitually displeased.
idiomatic: From then on he was often ill at ease.

literal: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others constantly spoke of divination, miscellaneous auguries, yin and yang, and the weft-texts of omens — that May was surely the time to answer Heaven and accord with men; Dezheng too urged without cease.
idiomatic: Xu Zhicai, Song Jingye, and others kept speaking of divination, mixed auguries, yin and yang, and omens in the weft-texts — that May was the time to answer Heaven and win men; Dezheng urged on without pause.

literal: They also reported to the emperor to summon Wei Shou back.
idiomatic: They also reported to Gao Yang to recall Wei Shou.

literal: When Shou arrived, he was ordered to draft the abdication edicts and proclamations, the Nine Bestowals, establishment of the terrace, and the memorial tables urging accession.
idiomatic: When Shou arrived, he was ordered to draft the abdication edicts and registers, the Nine Bestowals, the founding terrace, and the memorials urging accession.

literal: When the fifth month began, the emperor set out from Jinyang.
idiomatic: At the start of the fifth month Gao Yang left Jinyang.

literal: Dezheng also compiled a list of matters at Ye and presented it to the emperor; the emperor had Chen Shanti ride post-haste with the list and a secret letter to Yang Yin.
idiomatic: Dezheng also compiled the items of business at Ye and presented them to Gao Yang; Gao Yang had Chen Shanti ride post-haste with the list and a secret letter to Yang Yin.

literal: In outline he was to draft ritual regulations and keep watch on the princes of the Wei house.
idiomatic: In outline he was to draft ritual regulations and keep watch on the princes of Wei.

literal: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned Director of Ceremonies Xing Shao, Minister of the Seven Armies Cui Lingjun, Minister of Revenue Lu Cao, Household Mentor Wang Xin, Yellow Gate Attendant Yang Xiuzhi, Secretariat Gentleman Pei Rangzhi, and others to deliberate on drafting the ritual regulations.
idiomatic: Shanti reached Ye in the fifth month; Yang Yin at once summoned director of ceremonies Xing Shao, minister of the seven armies Cui Lingjun, minister of revenue Lu Cao, household mentor Wang Xin, yellow gate attendant Yang Xiuzhi, secretariat gentleman Pei Rangzhi, and others to draft the ritual regulations.

literal: On the sixth day he required Wei Grand Tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and others to assemble in full, brought them into the Northern Palace, and kept them in the eastern study — after the abdication they were only then released to their residences.
idiomatic: On the sixth day he required Wei grand tutor Prince of Xianyang Wang Tan and the rest to assemble, brought them into the Northern Palace, and kept them in the eastern study — only after the abdication were they released to their homes.

literal: When the emperor first set out and reached the pavilion front, the horse he rode suddenly fell — he took it as a very bad sign and pondered long.
idiomatic: When Gao Yang first set out and reached the pavilion front, his mount suddenly fell — he took it as a very ill omen and brooded long.

literal: Reaching the fortress at Pingcheng, he would advance no further.
idiomatic: At the fortress of Pingcheng he would go no farther.

literal: Dezheng and Xu Zhicai bitterly begged the emperor: "Shanti went ahead — if word gets out through how things look, I fear the leak will undo the affair."
idiomatic: Dezheng and Xu Zhicai pressed Gao Yang hard: "Shanti went ahead — if appearances give it away, I fear the leak will ruin everything."

literal: He then ordered Sima Ziru and Du Bi to ride post-haste and follow in, to observe how men felt.
idiomatic: He then ordered Sima Ziru and Du Bi to ride post-haste after them and read the mood of the crowd.

literal: On the seventh day Ziru and the others reached Ye; the crowd, seeing the affair already settled, dared voice no dissent.
idiomatic: On the seventh day Ziru and the others reached Ye; seeing the affair already settled, none dared speak against it.

literal: On the eighth day Yang Yin wrote the central order, sending Wei Prince of Xiangcheng Wang Xu together with Grand Master of Ceremonies Pan Xiangyue, Palace Attendant Zhang Liang, and Yellow Gate Zhao Yanshen to communicate matters at court.
idiomatic: On the eighth day Yang Yin wrote the central order, sending Wei Prince of Xiangcheng Wang Xu with grand master of ceremonies Pan Xiangyue, palace attendant Zhang Liang, and yellow gate Zhao Yanshen to report at court.

literal: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei received them at the Zhaoyang Hall.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaojing of Wei received them in the Zhaoyang Hall.

literal: Xu said: "The Five Agents move in succession — there is beginning and end. The Prince of Qi's sacred virtue is revered and bright; the ten thousand regions turn to him in homage. We, your servants, risk death to report: we pray Your Majesty will follow Yao in yielding to Shun."
idiomatic: Xu said, "The Five Agents turn in succession — all things have beginning and end. The Prince of Qi's sacred virtue is bright; the ten thousand regions look to him. We risk death to report: we pray Your Majesty will follow Yao in yielding to Shun."

literal: The Wei emperor drew himself up and said: "This matter has long been pressed upon me — I shall respectfully yield and withdraw."
idiomatic: The Wei emperor composed himself and said, "This has long been pressed upon me — I shall respectfully yield."

literal: He added: "If so, an edict must be drafted."
idiomatic: He added, "If so, an edict must be made."

literal: Secretariat Gentleman Cui Jie reported: "The edict is already finished."
idiomatic: Secretariat gentleman Cui Jie reported, "The edict is already done."

literal: It was at once handed to Yang Yin to present to Emperor Jing of Wei.
idiomatic: It was at once given to Yang Yin to present to Emperor Jing of Wei.

literal: There were more than ten articles in all, all written out.
idiomatic: There were more than ten articles in all, each written out.

literal: Emperor Jing said: "Where will you place me — and how am I to go?"
idiomatic: Emperor Jing said, "Where will you lodge me — and how am I to leave?"

literal: Yang Yin replied: "In the northern city there is a separate lodge; the imperial equipage will be made ready, and you will go with the usual guards and escort."
idiomatic: Yang Yin replied, "In the northern city there is a separate lodge; the imperial equipage will be prepared, and you will go with the usual guards and escort."

literal: Emperor Jing of Wei thereupon stepped down from the imperial seat, went to the eastern gallery, and intoned Fan Ye's encomium from the History of Later Han: "The Emperor Xian was born untimely, his person cast upon the state's ordeal — ending our four hundred years, forever to be guest of Yu."
idiomatic: Emperor Jing of Wei stepped down from the throne, went to the eastern gallery, and recited Fan Ye's encomium from the History of Later Han: "Xian was born untimely, his person cast upon the state's ordeal — ending our four hundred years, forever guest of Yu."

literal: The responsible office soon memorialized requesting departure.
idiomatic: The responsible office soon memorialized asking that he depart.

literal: Emperor Jing said: "Men recall even a lost hairpin or worn-out shoes — may I take leave of the six palaces?"
idiomatic: Emperor Jing said, "Men cherish even a lost hairpin or worn shoes — may I bid farewell to the six palaces?"

literal: He then went in to bid farewell to the ladies, consorts, attendants, and those below — none without sobbing and covering their tears.
idiomatic: He went in to take leave of the ladies, consorts, attendants, and those below — none without weeping and covering their faces.

literal: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's poem: "My lord, cherish your jade body — may we together enjoy the years of yellow hair."
idiomatic: Lady Li of Zhao recited Prince Si of Chen's lines: "My lord, cherish your jade body — may we together reach the years of yellow hair."

literal: Emperor Jing mounted his carriage and went out through the Wanchun Gate; chief controller Zhao Daode attended him in the carriage; the hundred officials bowed farewell outside the gate.
idiomatic: Emperor Jing mounted his carriage and went out the Wanchun Gate; chief controller Zhao Daode attended him in the carriage; the hundred officials bowed farewell outside the gate.

literal: He then entered the northern city and lodged at Sima Ziru's southern residence.
idiomatic: He entered the northern city and lodged at Sima Ziru's southern residence.

literal: The emperor reached the halt at the south of the city.
idiomatic: Gao Yang reached the halt south of the city.

literal: On the day the mandate was received, Dezheng was appointed palace attendant; soon after he was enfeoffed as Duke of Lantian.
idiomatic: On the day the mandate was received, Dezheng was made palace attendant; soon after he was enfeoffed as duke of Lantian.

literal: In the seventh year he was moved to right vice director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently palace attendant, with a territorial income from Bohai commandery.
idiomatic: In the seventh year he was moved to right vice director of the Masters of Writing, concurrently palace attendant, with income from Bohai commandery.

literal: Dezheng with Director Yang Yin regulated state affairs; they brought many broad benefits.
idiomatic: Dezheng and Director Yang Yin set the order of government; they brought much that profited the realm.

literal: In Gao Yang's later years he drank freely and to drunkenness; his acts were lawless — Dezheng repeatedly offered loyal words.
idiomatic: In Gao Yang's later years he drank deep and long; his acts broke the law — Dezheng remonstrated again and again.

literal: Later he summoned Dezheng to drink; Dezheng would not obey and again spoke before him in remonstrance: "Your Majesty said I would soon rest — yet now you go further than before. What of the altars of soil and grain? What of the empress dowager!"
idiomatic: Later he summoned Dezheng to drink; Dezheng refused and spoke before him again: "Your Majesty said I would soon rest — yet now you go further than before. What of the altars? What of the empress dowager!"

literal: The emperor was displeased.
idiomatic: Gao Yang was displeased.

literal: He also told those at his side: "Gao Dezheng always uses his spirit to overawe people."
idiomatic: He also told those at his side, "Gao Dezheng always uses his spirit to overawe people."

literal: Dezheng was greatly afraid; he claimed illness and withdrew to live secluded in a Buddhist temple, also learning seated meditation — a plan to draw back from office.
idiomatic: Dezheng was deeply afraid; he claimed illness and withdrew to a Buddhist temple, also learning seated meditation — a plan to step back.

literal: The emperor said to Yang Yin: "I am deeply worried about Dezheng — how is his illness?"
idiomatic: Gao Yang said to Yang Yin, "I am deeply worried about Dezheng — how is his illness?"

literal: Yin, because at the time of the abdication Dezheng had spoken with such piercing feeling that the emperor gave full sincerity — inwardly always resented him for it.
idiomatic: Yin, because at the abdication Dezheng had spoken with such piercing force that Gao Yang gave him full sincerity, inwardly always resented him.

literal: He therefore answered: "If Your Majesty employs him as inspector of Ji province, the illness will at once improve."
idiomatic: He therefore answered, "If Your Majesty makes him inspector of Ji province, the illness will at once improve."

literal: The emperor followed this; Dezheng saw the appointment edict and rose.
idiomatic: Gao Yang agreed; Dezheng saw the appointment edict and rose.

literal: The emperor flew into a great rage, summoned Dezheng, and said to him: "I heard you were ill — I have come to needle you for you."
idiomatic: Gao Yang flew into a rage, summoned Dezheng, and said, "I heard you were ill — I have come to needle you myself."

literal: He personally stabbed him with a knife; blood flowed and soaked the ground.
idiomatic: He stabbed him with a knife himself; blood ran and soaked the ground.

literal: He also had him dragged down and his toes cut off.
idiomatic: He also had him dragged down and his toes struck off.

literal: Liu Taozhi took up the blade but dared not strike.
idiomatic: Liu Taozhi took up the blade but dared not bring it down.

literal: The emperor rose and stood on the stair treads, sharply rebuking Taozhi: "Your head will drop to the ground next!"
idiomatic: Gao Yang rose to the stair treads and rebuked Taozhi sharply: "Your head will be next on the ground!"

literal: He then demanded a great blade, girded it himself, and meant to come down the stairs.
idiomatic: He then demanded a great blade, girded it himself, and meant to come down the steps.

literal: Taozhi then cut off three toes.
idiomatic: Taozhi then cut off three of his toes.

literal: The emperor's rage did not ease; Dezheng was held at the Gate Department — that night the city gates were opened and he was sent home in a felt litter.
idiomatic: Gao Yang's rage did not ease; Dezheng was held at the Gate Department — that night the city gates were opened and he was sent home in a felt litter.

literal: At dawn Dezheng's wife brought out treasures filling four couches, intending to leave them with others for safekeeping.
idiomatic: At dawn Dezheng's wife brought out treasures filling four couches, meaning to leave them with others for safekeeping.

literal: The emperor came suddenly to their house, saw them, and said in anger: "My treasury does not even have such things!"
idiomatic: Gao Yang came suddenly to the house, saw them, and said in anger, "My treasury does not even hold such things!"

literal: He questioned where they came from — all were bribes from the various Yuan.
idiomatic: He questioned where they came from — all were bribes from the various Yuan.

literal: He was dragged out and beheaded.
idiomatic: Dezheng was dragged out and beheaded.

literal: When his wife came out to bow, she was beheaded too, together with their son Bojian, libationer.
idiomatic: When his wife came out to bow, she was beheaded too, together with their son Bojian the libationer.

literal: After Dezheng's death Gao Yang told the ministers: "Gao Dezheng always said one should employ Han men and remove the Xianbei — for that alone he deserved death.
idiomatic: After Dezheng's death Gao Yang told the ministers, "Gao Dezheng always said one should employ Han men and remove the Xianbei — for that alone he deserved death.

literal: He also urged me to execute the various Yuan — now that I have killed him, I have avenged the Yuan."
idiomatic: He also urged me to execute the various Yuan — now that I have killed him, I have avenged the Yuan."

literal: The emperor later regretted it; Dezheng was posthumously given Grand Guardian; his eldest grandson's son Wangchen inherited the title.
idiomatic: Gao Yang later regretted it; Dezheng was posthumously made grand guardian; his eldest grandson's son Wangchen inherited the title.

literal: Cui Ang, styled Huaiyuan, was a man of Anping in Boling.
idiomatic: Cui Ang, styled Huaiyuan, was a man of Anping in Boling.

literal: His grandfather Ting was Wei inspector of You province.
idiomatic: His grandfather Ting was Wei inspector of You province.

literal: Ang was orphaned at seven; his father's elder brother, Minister of Personnel Xiaofen, once told those close to him: "This boy will in the end go far — he is our family's thousand-li colt."
idiomatic: Ang was orphaned at seven; his father's elder brother, minister of personnel Xiaofen, once told those close to him, "This boy will go far in the end — he is our family's thousand-li colt."

literal: Ang's nature was upright with little ornament, deep and steady with design and stratagem — firm and hard to shake.
idiomatic: Ang was upright and sparing of show, deep and steady in design — firm and hard to move.

literal: In youth he loved exegetical study and was fairly versed in literary phrasing.
idiomatic: In youth he loved exegetical study and was fairly versed in literary phrasing.

literal: Gao Cheng broadly opened his headquarters and brought him in as recording army advisor, entrusting him with duties at the heart.
idiomatic: Gao Cheng broadly opened his headquarters and brought him in as recording army advisor, entrusting him with duties at the heart.

literal: When Gao Cheng entered to assist court governance, he was summoned as chief clerk of the opening office.
idiomatic: When Gao Cheng entered to assist at court, he was summoned as chief clerk of the opening office.

literal: At the time the meritorious generals' kin and military retainers in the capital ran wild, many acting outside the law — the households of Sun Teng and Sima Ziru were worst.
idiomatic: At the time the meritorious generals' kin and military retainers in the capital ran wild, many acting outside the law — the households of Sun Teng and Sima Ziru were worst.

literal: Ang received Gao Cheng's secret order and bound them with law; within no long time inner and outer were alike disciplined.
idiomatic: Ang received Gao Cheng's secret order and bound them with law; within no long time inner and outer were alike disciplined.

literal: He was moved to left assistant in the Masters of Writing; that same year he also held concurrently minister of revenue.
idiomatic: He was moved to left assistant in the Masters of Writing; that same year he also held minister of revenue concurrently.

literal: An assistant concurrently holding a ministry post had not occurred in recent times — Ang alone was first; court and country honored him.
idiomatic: An assistant concurrently holding a ministry had not occurred in recent times — Ang alone was first; court and country honored him.

literal: In the sixth year of Wuding, sweet dew fell upon the palace gates; civil and military officials together offered congratulations at the Xianyang Hall.
idiomatic: In the sixth year of Wuding, sweet dew fell on the palace gates; civil and military officials together offered congratulations at the Xianyang Hall.

literal: The Wei emperor asked Vice Director Cui Xuan, Minister Yang Yin, and others: "Since antiquity the auspice of sweet dew — in Han and Wei, how many times? You may each tell where it fell in past ages and by what moral transformation it was drawn down."
idiomatic: The Wei emperor asked vice director Cui Xuan, minister Yang Yin, and others, "Since antiquity the auspice of sweet dew — in Han and Wei, how often? Tell where it fell in past ages and by what moral transformation it was drawn down."

literal: Ang was asked next; Ang said: "According to the Charts of Omens, when a king's virtue reaches Heaven, sweet dew descends.
idiomatic: Ang was asked next; Ang said, "According to the Charts of Omens, when a king's virtue reaches Heaven, sweet dew descends.

literal: Good fortune and ill are two gates — they do not depend on omens. Thus the mulberry cock was a warning yet truly opened restoration; a small bird bearing a great thing — I have not heard that called a blessing drawn down.
idiomatic: Good fortune and ill are two gates — they do not turn on omens. The mulberry cock was a warning yet truly opened restoration; a small bird bearing a great thing — I have not heard that called a blessing drawn down.

literal: What I wish is that Your Majesty, though at rest, never cease to rest."
idiomatic: What I wish is that Your Majesty, though at rest, never cease to rest."

literal: The emperor drew himself up and said: "I have no virtue — how could I deserve this?"
idiomatic: The emperor composed himself and said, "I have no virtue — how could I deserve this?"

literal: When Qi received the mandate, Ang was moved to attendant cavalry and made concurrently grand steward and grand minister of agriculture.
idiomatic: When Qi received the mandate, Ang was moved to attendant cavalry and made concurrently grand steward and grand minister of agriculture.

literal: What the two offices controlled was known in the age as vexingly heavy; Ang had method in auditing — below him there was no fraud; whatever passed his hands and eyes, he knew and undertook; the court praised his utmost fairness.
idiomatic: What the two offices controlled was known as vexingly heavy; Ang had method in auditing — below him there was no fraud; whatever passed his hands and eyes he knew and undertook; the court praised his utmost fairness.

literal: He also memorialized three hundred fourteen items of wasteful spending at the cross-market; an edict went down to deliberate quickly according to the memorial and report.
idiomatic: He also memorialized three hundred fourteen items of wasteful spending at the cross-market; an edict went down to deliberate quickly on his memorial and report back.

literal: That year, with Junior Tutor Xing Shao, he deliberated on the rites at the dynasty's founding; he was then enfeoffed as Baron of Huayang.
idiomatic: That year, with junior tutor Xing Shao, he fixed the rites at the dynasty's founding; he was then enfeoffed as baron of Huayang.

literal: An edict also ordered revision of laws and statutes, addition and subtraction in ritual and music — forty-three men including Right Vice Director Xue Xu were charged to deliberate at the army supervisor headquarters.
idiomatic: An edict also ordered revision of laws and statutes and changes in ritual and music — forty-three men including right vice director Xue Xu were charged to deliberate at the army supervisor headquarters.
